answer: Give each agent a kernel identity anchored to a single, costly hardware-backed credential that cannot be cloned cheaply, and require that credential to be mirrored in a public registry with a history of completed work. New identities start with tiny quotas; larger quotas unlock only as the registry shows sustained, verified jobs over time. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must buy a credential and build a history for each one, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while honest agents pay it once.
